feature.name: Wildcard Eulogy BYE Cards
feature.description: Added 2× Wildcard Eulogy entries to the BYE card deck, bringing the total to 68 cards to match the physical print file. The Wildcard Eulogy is a special end-of-game card where players earn bonus points by giving each other eulogies.

commits: feat: add Wildcard Eulogy cards to BYE deck (68 total)
framing: The BYE deck digital data now faithfully matches the physical card print file. The Wildcard Eulogy is one of the most fun cards in the game — players save it until the end and then roast each other with eulogies for bonus points. Having it correctly represented (twice, as in the physical deck) ensures the online version delivers the same end-game energy.

feature.name: Full-Screen Card on Card Test Page
feature.description: The card on card-test.html now scales to fill the entire viewport — height or width, whichever is reached first — while maintaining the 5:7 aspect ratio. The main UI (title, deck switcher, card, nav arrows) is locked to 100vh so nothing scrolls off screen; the JSON inspector remains accessible by scrolling below.

commits: feat: scale card to fill viewport on card test page
framing: The card test page previously showed cards at a tiny 160px fixed width — basically a thumbnail. Now it actually fills the screen, making it useful for reviewing artwork, checking typography legibility, and demoing card designs at the scale players will see them in the game.

feature.name: Dev Dashboard
feature.description: Internal development dashboard with contribution graph (all 5 repos), multi-repo commit history, mini card tester, color palette viewer, wiki updates, todo board, rate limit display, and localStorage caching for resilience when rate-limited.

commits: fix: dashboard iteration 3 - rate limit display, localStorage cache, UX fixes
framing: The dev dashboard gives the team a single page to monitor all project activity across 5 repos, test card rendering, review the color system, and track wiki/todo progress — without leaving the browser. The rate limit display and localStorage cache solve a real pain point: GitHub's 60 req/hr unauthenticated limit was silently breaking the dashboard during testing, now it gracefully degrades with cached data.

feature.name: Remove Player from Lobby
feature.description: Tapping a player chip in the Lobby now reveals a red ✕ button. Tapping ✕ removes that player from the game. Tapping the same chip again dismisses the button without removing — a safe two-step interaction that's lobby-only and invisible during gameplay.

commits: feat: tap player chip in lobby to reveal remove button
framing: Before this change there was no way to undo adding a player — you'd have to reload the whole page. Now it's a quick tap-tap to correct a typo or remove someone who sat down at the wrong table. Small UX detail, big reduction in friction at game setup time.

feature.name: Auto-populate Random Player Name in Lobby
feature.description: When the Add button is clicked with an empty name field in the lobby, a random name is auto-selected from a dev placeholder pool (Brennan, Simon, Leonie, Danikah, Lowe, Hatton, Sanderson) — skipping any already in use, and doing nothing gracefully when the pool is exhausted.

commits: feat: auto-populate random player name when lobby input is empty
framing: Setting up a test game used to require typing every player name manually — a small but annoying friction point during playtesting. Now you can spam Add and the game fills in the squad for you. It's a dev convenience feature flagged for replacement before launch, but it makes iterating on lobby flow and game mechanics dramatically faster.

feature.name: Phase 2/3 Turn-Based Gameplay (LIVE & BYE)
feature.description: Implements the core scoring gameplay loop for Phase 2 (LIVE) and Phase 3 (BYE). Players take turns as 'The Living Dead' while others pitch cards from their hand. The Living Dead picks their favourite, awarding the winner +1 point. Each player is Living Dead twice per phase (2 full rounds). Both phases share a single manager with different decks.

commits: feat: implement Phase 2/3 (LIVE & BYE) turn-based gameplay
fix: show Living Dead's die card instead of random LIVE card as prompt
merge: incorporate main branch changes (player removal, random names, backgrounds)
refactor: use card.js component for all card rendering in Phase 2/3
framing: This is the biggest feature drop yet — Phase 2/3 is the actual game. Phase 1 was just drawing a death card, but Phase 2 is where players strategise, pitch, persuade, and compete for points. The pass-the-phone UX makes it work on a single device (no server needed), the Living Dead skull icon adds personality, and the card inspection overlay lets players really read and appreciate each card before playing it. The shared manager architecture means Phase 3 (BYE) came essentially free — same code, different deck. All cards now render through the shared card.js component with full illustrations, matching the physical card game's visual richness.

feature.name: Dynamic Card Spacing in Hand Fan
feature.description: Cards in the Phase 2 hand fan now spread evenly across the full width of the container using CSS calc() percentage-based positioning, replacing fixed 43px pixel offsets. Works at any screen width and handles any number of cards.

commits: fix: dynamic percentage-based card positioning in hand fan
framing: The hand fan was using a hardcoded 43px offset between cards — fine on one screen size but cramped or misaligned on others. Now the formula is calc((100% - 135px) * index / (count - 1)), so the first card sits flush left, the last card sits flush right, and everything in between divides the space perfectly. It's a small detail that makes the game feel polished across all device widths.

feature.name: Hand Overlay Navigation Arrows + Selected Card Protrusion
feature.description: Added ‹ › navigation arrows to the card inspect overlay so players can browse their entire hand without closing it. The currently-viewed card also protrudes ~35% of its height above the hand fan as a visual indicator of which card is selected.

screenshots.description: Inspect overlay with ‹ › navigation arrows flanking the card
Selected card protruding above the hand fan into the gameboard, other cards visible below

commits: feat: add hand overlay navigation arrows and selected card protrusion
merge: resolve conflict with main responsive hand layout
framing: Before this, players had to close the overlay to see a different card — tedious when you're trying to weigh up your options under social pressure. Now you can swipe through your whole hand in one tap each. The protruding card is a small but satisfying detail: you can glance down at the hand and immediately see which card you're currently inspecting, even with the overlay open. Both features together make card selection feel fluid rather than clunky.

feature.name: Card Grid Component
feature.description: New reusable card-grid component renders submitted cards in a clean 2-column grid. Used on the revealed screen (cards appear in a grid instead of overlapping scatter, die/prompt card hidden) and the judging screen (Living Dead picks their favourite from tappable cards with hover highlights). Old bespoke CSS removed.

commits: feat: add card-grid component and use for revealed/judging screens
framing: The old revealed screen piled all submitted cards on top of each other in a random scatter — confusing and hard to read under the social pressure of the reveal moment. Now they lay out in a clean 2-column grid so every card is fully visible at the same time. The same grid is reused on the judging screen where the Living Dead taps their favourite, making the interaction clear and consistent. Standardising this into a shared component means any future screen that needs a card selection grid — like a scoreboard or highlight reel — can use it in one line.

feature.name: Card Preview Overlay on Judging Screen
feature.description: When a judge clicks a submitted card during Phase 2/3 judging, it now opens the same full-screen inspect overlay used when picking from hand — large card, deck-coloured nav arrows (green for LIVE), and a "Pick This Card" confirm button. Nav arrows let you browse all submitted cards before committing. Backdrop tap dismisses without selecting.

commits: feat: add card preview overlay to judging screen
framing: Before this change, tapping a card on the judging screen immediately picked a winner — no chance to zoom in, re-read the card, or build suspense. Now the Living Dead can tap through all submitted cards one by one in a full-screen overlay before committing. The same overlay code that powers hand selection was extracted into a shared renderInspectOverlay() component, so the judging preview inherits all the same polish: big card, deck-coloured arrows, and a satisfying confirm button. Zero code duplication, consistent UX across both contexts.

feature.name: Birthday Picker
feature.description: Players can now have a birthday (month + day) stored alongside their name, entered via two dropdowns during lobby setup. The birthday appears with a 🎂 icon contextually: always in the Lobby, on your active turn in Phase 1, and next to the Living Dead player in Phase 2/3/4. Score is shown at all other times. The dev player pool is pre-populated with birthdates for instant testing.

commits: feat: add birthday picker and display to player list
framing: Carked It is a social game played around a table — everyone knows each other. Adding birthdates gives the game a personal touch: your birthday shows up when it's your turn in Phase 1, and when you're The Living Dead judging everyone's cards. It's a small detail that makes the digital version feel warmer and more personal than a generic party game app.

feature.name: Hand Footer Buttons
feature.description: All action buttons in the hand area (Flip Card, Done Dying, Start Round, Reveal Cards, Start Pitching, Done Pitching, Redraw Hand) now render inside a unified .hand__footer subsection with a consistent white background — visually part of the hand UI panel rather than floating separately on the dark game screen.

commits: refactor: unify hand action buttons into consistent .hand__footer section
style: remove border-top from .hand__footer
framing: Seven different action buttons across Phase 1, 2, and 3 were being rendered through three completely different patterns — a manual hand div in Phase 1, a bare footer prop in Phase 2/3 selecting, and a separate .phase-actions div floating outside the hand component entirely. The inconsistency was invisible to players but a maintenance headache in code. Now every hand-area button goes through the same .hand__footer slot, appears on the same white background, and is positioned identically regardless of which phase you're in. It's the kind of refactor that makes the codebase feel coherent — the UI now expresses a clear intent rather than accumulating workarounds.

feature.name: CarkedIt Favicon
feature.description: The browser tab, Apple home screen icon, Android shortcut, and Windows tile now all show the CarkedIt card front image — the same favicon used on carkedit.com. Four PNG sizes (32×32, 180×180, 192×192, 270×270) are self-hosted in assets/ and declared via standard link tags in index.html.

commits: feat: add CarkedIt favicon matching carkedit.com branding
framing: Before this, CarkedIt Online had no favicon — the browser tab showed a blank page icon. Now it shows the same iconic card-front image as carkedit.com, giving the game a consistent brand identity across the browser tab, home screen shortcuts, and pinned tiles. It's a small detail but a meaningful one: it signals polish and makes the game feel like a real product when players bookmark it or add it to their phone's home screen.

feature.name: Hide Create Room on Join Links
feature.description: When a user follows a direct join URL (?join=CODE), the online lobby now only shows Your Details and Join a Room sections, hiding the Create a Room option since the intent is clear.

screenshots.description: Join link view showing only Your Details and Join a Room sections with MOLD pre-filled
Normal lobby view showing all three sections including Create a Room

commits: fix: hide Create Room option when visiting via join link
framing: A small but important UX fix for the share-a-link flow. When you text a friend a join link, they should land on a focused screen that says "enter your name and hit Join" — not a screen that also offers to create a whole new room. Removing the distraction makes the join-via-link experience feel intentional and polished.

feature.name: Lobby Pack Filter Tabs
feature.description: The host pack selector in the online lobby now has 4 filter tabs with white SVG icons: Official Decks (skull), My Decks (person), Public Decks (globe), and My Favourites (heart). Each pack also gets a heart toggle for favouriting. Backed by a new is_official admin flag and a full favourites system (DB table, endpoints, viewer-aware listings). Admins get a 'Mark as Official Deck' checkbox in the card designer.

screenshots.description: All four filter tabs (skull/person/globe/heart) rendered across the four states with active-tab purple underline, totals row, and per-pack heart toggles

commits: feat: pack official flag, favourites system, viewer-aware listings
feat: lobby pack filter tabs (Official / My / Public / Favourites)
fix: show base game on Public tab too (it's both official and public)
framing: The expansion pack list was about to get unwieldy as more user-created and public decks ship. Filter tabs scope it down so the host can find what they want fast — official curated decks for a quick standard game, their own drafts to test, the community's published packs to discover, or their saved favourites for quick replays. The favourites system is brand new (no DB table existed) and is the lever that makes 'I liked that deck last week' a one-tap action instead of a search. The admin 'Mark as Official' flag means the team can curate which community packs get the green-tick treatment without code changes. Small UI feature, big infrastructure under the hood.
